newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-TAYLOR SAYS NO TO WORLD CHAMPIONSHIP TAG.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-TAYLOR SAYS NO TO WORLD CHAMPIONSHIP TAG.

text.p: Australian captain Mark Taylor has rejected the 'unofficial world championship' tag attached to his team's forthcoming three-test tour of South Africa.
Taylor said on arrival on Monday: "I don't like labels and at the end of this series I won't be handing out the world champion label and neither will Hansie Cronje.
"We've had a good run and beaten a lot of sides, but one side we haven't beaten is South Africa. They tied 1-1 with us in Australia in 1993 and we did the same in South Africa in 1994."
Taylor's squad of 14 was criticised for the omission of big names like Michael Slater and Ricky Ponting, but he was adamant that the best players had travelled to South Africa.
"At the end of the day the guys picked themselves. We settled on a side at the Melbourne test against the West Indies and that team won us the series with the win in Adelaide.
"Basically we've brought the 12 from that game and added Jason Gillespie and Matthew Elliott, both of whom played earlier in the series in any case."
Taylor said that his own form against the West Indies was poor, "But that can happen against a team with a good new ball attack. I'm looking forward to a new challenge."

He also played down the "sledging" controversy which soured the final test in Perth. "It's a non-issue. If it gets bad I'll step in, but this series is between two sides who enjoy playing against each other and I can't forsee any problems.
Australia begin their tour on Thursday with a one-day match against a Nicky Oppenheimer XI at Randjesfontein.
